text: You’re in a bustling crowd, trying to get somewhere. You just want to keep moving, a simple, reasonable goal.
But suddenly, the flow slows. You push gently, then a little harder, trying to carve out your path, but it’s no use.
Frustration builds. You scan for the blockage, blaming the slow person ahead, or the group dawdling by the exit.
But the real problem isn't one person; it’s the system itself. When density hits a critical point, small individual movements create tiny, cascading blockages.
This creates a feedback loop: everyone trying to move faster just increases the local density and friction, paradoxically slowing everyone down.
Now, you see the crowd not as individuals, but as a fluid system. You can anticipate the waves, conserve energy, and move with the flow instead of fighting it.
